notes: Genuine test/retest on the measurement itself, not a re-read of the POS log: Priya re-timed the same 10 already-collected orders from the counter's recorded security-camera video (register-paid stamp to name-call, same operational definition as the collection plan), twice, two days apart, blind to her first pass -- the first-pass timing sheet stayed in a sealed envelope, and the video was re-cued from the start each time so the second pass carried no memory of the first. Items are real order_ids from wait-times.csv, picked to span the observed range (6.0 to 11.1 min); first readings match the recorded dataset values, second readings are independent re-timings and differ from the first on all 10 items (0.1-0.3 min apart, both directions -- genuine human re-read noise, not a discretization artifact). Gauge increment is the video timestamp overlay's resolution, 0.1 min. USL 5.0 is the customer walk-away line (VoC S4); no LSL -- a fast drink has no lower limit, so the engine names its denominator as study variation, not tolerance. Resolution pre-check: 0.1-min increments on the 5.1-minute observed span (ratio 2.0%, well inside the 1/10 ceiling). Engine verdict: repeatability 8.94% (s_repeat 0.120 min against 6*s_study = 8.079) -- acceptable (<=10%). Single-operator repeatability only -- the caveat the engine prints is part of the record.
gauge_name: Counter security-camera video, timestamp overlay read to 0.1 min
